catalogue_requests.reason: cap.measure.voltage.v1 binds instrument.dmm, instrument.smu or sensor and returns a voltage in V. The rp2daq ADC returns raw 12-bit counts, and the clone gives only an approximate count-to-volt relation (README.md:100); the device kind is io.gpio. The extension carries the raw mean count, the sample count and the channel mask.
catalogue_requests.summary: Capture one ADC block from the built-in 12-bit ADC and report its mean raw count.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class describes configuring a PWM slice. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 has a mode enum (digital/analog/pwm) but one numeric value field: a digital level is 0 to 1 while a PWM duty value is 0 to 65535, and the class cannot carry the firmware's wrap, clock-divider and phase-correct inputs. The extension carries the firmware's pwm_configure_pair and pwm_set_value parameters.
catalogue_requests.summary: Configure one PWM slice and set the duty value of one GPIO.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class configures an A4988-compatible stepper. The motion classes bind robot.arm or motion.axis and use radians; the clone states no gear ratio or kinematics, only nanostep counts (include/stepper.c:200-246). The extension carries the firmware's stepper_init fields.
catalogue_requests.summary: Initialize one A4988-compatible stepper on its direction, step, endswitch and enable GPIO pins.

catalogue_requests.reason: The native move target is a nanostep count (1/256 microstep) with no rad conversion stated in the clone, and the device kind is io.gpio; cap.motion.joint_position.v1 binds robot.arm or motion.axis and expects joint positions in radians. The extension carries the firmware's absolute or relative nanostep move.
catalogue_requests.summary: Move one initialized stepper to an absolute or relative nanostep position.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm, robot.mobile_base or motion.axis and asks for a deceleration in m/s2. The rp2daq safe state is not a motion deceleration: it holds each initialized stepper at its current nanostep position, zeroes the configured PWM outputs and drives the configured GPIO outputs low. The extension is the empty-input safe-state action SAFE-045 accepts for this R2 package.
catalogue_requests.summary: Hold every initialized stepper at its current position, zero PWM outputs and drive configured GPIO outputs low.

MINIMAL REPRO OF THE GATE DEFECT:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=MHS/sdk/src python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; from mhs.driver.upstream import UpstreamTree, class_surface; s=class_surface(UpstreamTree(Path('labs/filipdominec/rp2daq'), commit='7744f34811d1b3722d30e6efd66205215405fe60'), 'rp2daq:Rp2daq', hint_file='rp2daq.py'); print(sorted(s.names), s.open)"
prints ['__init__', '_i', 'quit'] []: the AST surface of the card entry class has no command attributes and no open fallback. The documented methods adc, gpio_out, gpio_highz, pwm_configure_pair, pwm_set_value, stepper_init, stepper_move and stepper_status are generated from the C firmware and attached to the Rp2daq object at construction by Rp2daq_internals._register_commands (rp2daq.py:110-121: setattr(self._e, cmd_name, types.MethodType(...))). G7's class_surface records a dynamic setattr only when it appears in the native class's own methods; this setattr is in Rp2daq_internals, so surface.open stays empty and every dynamically attached command becomes a G7.NOT_UPSTREAM error ('a fake may only implement what the upstream class has') instead of the MAYBE_ABSENT warning G7 uses for a class with an external base or __getattr__. Following the setattr/Rp2daq_internals chain, or letting the card declare dynamic commands, would fix the gate. The package cannot fix this without editing the read-only clone or bypassing the Recorder, which would be a gate workaround.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the helper hint is PythonObjectDriver, but the command methods do not exist on the class at scan time; the package is a direct Driver over the card's entry symbol rp2daq:Rp2daq, consistent with the card's direct-driver decision and with the upstream object-with-methods shape.

What the package implements: reads gpio_pin and gpio_level (driver state, because the firmware has no configuration read-back), adc_mean (one ADC block on channel 0), stepper_position and stepper_moving (stepper 0); writes gpio_pin and gpio_level; extension actions for an ADC block, PWM configuration and duty, stepper initialization and absolute/relative stepper move; the @estop and the safe-state action both call stepper_status(0), hold every initialized stepper at its current position, zero the configured PWM outputs and drive the configured GPIO outputs low. All numeric inputs have sourced limits from the clone, so site-limits.example.json was not needed and the exemplar copy was deleted. G1-G6 and G8 pass on the fake backend; the hardware factory native.py was never imported and no hardware was attached or run.

The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is {'kind': 'model', 'model_id': 'deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017', 'run_id': 'wC-010'}, reviewed_by is null, and no human reviewed or tested anything here. No MHS-Device level is claimed; the evidence is contract_checked on the fake only.

NOT COVERED: the hardware path through pyserial, tkinter and the C firmware tree; gpio_in, gpio_pull, gpio_on_change and gpio_out_seq; adc_stop and the raw ADC sample array (the driver reports only the mean count; the real adc returns blocksize samples, 1 to 8192, and the fake returns at most four placeholder samples); the full PWM/servo behaviour; steppers other than the tested single move; endswitch calibration and stop behaviour; and the upstream generated methods on real hardware. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; every number in fake.py is placeholder test data.
